campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 s08/s16/s32/k128: both c16 candidates eliminated (2026-09-09)
question: f3 found a step in depth-3 divergence between c16 and c20 - about 1% below, about 9% above. Two settings predict a boundary at exactly 16 sequences and were confounded there: VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_GROUP=16, which processes speculative rows in groups of at most 16 sequences, and max_cudagraph_capture_size=64 tokens, which is 16 sequences at depth 3. These three arms vary the group size at a fixed capture ceiling.
config: one B70, TP1, depth 3, draft INT4 head, pad off, capture 1-64 with ceiling 64, 2026-08-25 small-context suite, rungs 8/12/16/20/24/32/40, 10 passes each
finding: Neither the GDN speculative group size nor the capture ceiling sets the c16 step. Varying the group over a fourfold range and doubling the capture ceiling both leave the boundary between c16 and c20 exactly where it was. This is a double elimination, not an explanation: the step is now unexplained by any named candidate.
it_was_predicted: notes/2026-09-09-preliminary-the-gdn-group-is-probably-not-the-driver.md, written before these arms ran, argued the same from the 27B lane's existing mtp4 ladders at group sizes 0, 1, 4, 16 and 64: group 1 puts every sequence in its own group and should have been the worst arm but was among the quietest, and group 64 fits all 64 requests in one group and should have been near-exact but was not. That inference was weak - small, uncontrolled cells - and this is the controlled version of it.

what_remains.answered: k128 raised max_cudagraph_capture_size to 128 tokens - 32 sequences at depth 3 - at the default group size. The step did not move.
what_remains.intervention_verified: The server reports max_cudagraph_capture_size 128 and 'Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL): 17/17' against s16's 11, so the captured range really did double from 16 to 32 sequences.
what_remains.conclusion: The capture ceiling does not set the boundary either. Both candidates that sat at exactly 16 sequences are eliminated, each by moving its own knob and watching the step stay put.

the_bound_on_what_these_arms_can_settle: Five row-count thresholds are in play on this lane and only two sit at c16 - the RMSNorm from 16 rows, VLLM_XPU_FP16_LINEAR_ROWCHUNK at 32 rows and the FP16 vocabulary projection at 33 rows are all below it, at c4, c8 and c9 respectively. The ladder is already non-exact from c12, so something is happening before the step regardless of what the step is. Eliminating both c16 candidates would leave the step unexplained rather than explained.
a_side_result: These arms are the only ones on this lane to measure c40, and they found aggregate throughput is not monotone in concurrency: without speculation one card reads about 1595 tok/s at c32, 1360 at c40 and 1732 at c64. Two arms agree on c40 to 0.1%. Recorded in 2026-09-09-qwen35-4b-concurrency-throughput-matrix.json.
mtp0_control: The group size is a speculative-path setting and should do nothing without speculation, and it does nothing: the MTP0 ladders are exact through c24 in s08 and read 0.31-0.94% at c32 and 0.50-0.75% at c40 across the arms, with no ordering by group size.

what_this_leaves.the_step_is_unexplained: No remaining named mechanism sits at 16 sequences. Of the five row-count thresholds on this lane, three are below it - the RMSNorm at 16 rows (c4), FP16_LINEAR_ROWCHUNK at 32 rows (c8) and the FP16 vocabulary projection at 33 rows (c9) - and the two at c16 are now both ruled out.
what_this_leaves.it_may_not_be_one_mechanism: The ladder is already non-exact from c12, so something is contributing before the step. The 9B lane's account - that every row-count-dependent op contributes and no single one can be fixed to remove the effect - predicts a rate that grows as more thresholds are crossed rather than a boundary owned by one op. A step is still an odd shape for that, and it is not claimed to be explained.
what_this_leaves.predicted: notes/2026-09-09-preliminary-the-gdn-group-is-probably-not-the-driver.md recorded before these arms ran that under the 9B account both hypotheses were expected to fail, and that the arms were worth running to eliminate them by measurement rather than by inference. That is what happened.
